## Walkthrough

The XPath regex matcher adds optimized handling for large finite repetitions and updates work and storage accounting. Tests and benchmarks cover matching, captures, replacement, validators, resource limits, and multiple language interfaces. Documentation describes the updated behavior and limits.

### Changes

**Large finite XPath regex repetitions**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|:---|:---|
|**Compile repetition and follow metadata** <br> `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/compile.rs`, `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/pike.rs`|Compiled patterns record single-character runs and qualifying large repetitions. Repetition follow hints now include end anchors.|
|**Optimize backtracking repetition scans** <br> `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/match.rs`|The matcher scans eligible single-character runs, reuses scan results across search starts, checks follow constraints, and accounts for work credited to those scans.|
|**Reuse set-machine states with relative counts** <br> `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/sets.rs`|The set machine stores qualifying counts relative to offsets and tracks offset-dependent cache transitions, checkpoints, and storage.|
|**Validate matcher behavior and resource accounting** <br> `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/match.rs`, `crates/rdf-core/tests/native_regex_storage.rs`|Tests compare optimized and general matching paths, captures, and replacement results, and check behavior at compilation and matching storage limits.|
|**Exercise large counts across consumers and benchmarks** <br> `bindings/python/tests/*`, `crates/cli/tests/xpath_regex_cli.rs`, `crates/rdf-capi/tests/xpath_regex.rs`, `crates/rdf-wasm/*`, `crates/shapes/tests/native_xpath.rs`, `crates/shex/tests/native_xpath.rs`, `crates/rdf-core/benches/xsd_regex.rs`, `crates/testkit/src/text.rs`|Tests exercise large repetitions through query interfaces and validators. Benchmarks cover large-count matching and replacement; the testkit adds deterministic binary text fixtures.|
|**Update matcher limits and diagnostic documentation** <br> `crates/rdf-core/src/xsd_regex/xpath/mod.rs`, `docs/book/src/project/diagnostic-codes.md`, `docs/book/po/zh-Hans.po`|Documentation describes work accounting, count handling, operational limits, fixtures, and replacement work. The Chinese catalog updates related translations and references.|

**Shared sorted-table lookup**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|:---|:---|
|**Add and use sorted-table lookup** <br> `crates/lex/src/assoc.rs`, `crates/iri/src/idna.rs`|`assoc::get_sorted` adds borrowed-key binary search over caller-sorted tables. IDNA mapping uses it instead of a local lookup function.|

<!-- change_assessment_start -->
**Priority:** ➖ Normal







**Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~60 minutes

**Change:** Bug fix · **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium

### Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Caller as XPath regex caller
  participant Matcher as XPath regex matcher
  participant Backtracking as Backtracking machine
  participant Linear as Set and thread machines
  Caller->>Matcher: Match pattern and input
  Matcher->>Backtracking: Start non-backreference attempt
  Backtracking-->>Matcher: Return result or exceed allowance
  Matcher->>Linear: Continue with remaining fuel after allowance or live-state bound
  Linear-->>Matcher: Return result or operational limit
  Matcher-->>Caller: Return match result or error
```

**Possibly related PRs**

- [Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf#299](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf/pull/299): Introduced the shared regex engine used by SPARQL, SHACL, and ShEx, which this change modifies and tests.

**Explanation**

Issue `#467` requirements are implemented for the listed large-count shapes. The native matcher adds single-character and capture-chain scans, dated-maxima handling, and relative-count reuse. CLI, Python, C, WASM, validator, benchmark, and documentation changes cover the stated profiles and fixtures. The available evidence shows comparisons with the general backtracking matcher, but it does not establish that a randomized differential test against that matcher was run.
